series_books.title: How to Break Into Investment Banking
series_books.subtitle: The Ultimate Guide to Landing a Job on Wall Street: Networking Emails, Interview Answers, Resumes and Your First Year
series_books.description:
Wall Street hires the best, the brightest and the most prepared. This guide shows you how to be the most prepared person in the room.

Written for students and new grads, it covers the whole path into investment banking and the rest of the front office:

- How a bank is built: front, middle and back office, bulge bracket vs. middle market vs. boutique, and which group to pick
- The blueprint for getting in from a target school, a non-target school, a few years into your career, or business school
- Networking that works: who to contact, word-for-word emails and follow-ups, and what to ask on the call
- Interview questions with suggested answers: your story, why banking, accounting, valuation and brain teasers
- Resumes and cover letters that pass the 15-second test
- How to survive and stand out in your first internship or job, and what a real week looks like

At the back: a glossary of Wall Street terms, a reading list, an Excel shortcut cheat sheet and a financial ratio cheat sheet.

This 2026 edition updates pay, recruiting timing, bank names and tax figures from public sources. Part of the Ambitious Grads series.

series_books.title: How to Get a Job in Tech
series_books.subtitle: The Ultimate Guide to Silicon Valley Careers for New Grads: Pick a Role, Land the Interview, Answer the Questions and Understand Your Stock Options
series_books.description:
Tech jobs are some of the most sought-after jobs for new grads, and the path in is rarely written down. This guide writes it down.

It starts with the three choices that shape everything else (company stage, sector and role) and walks you through each role that drives growth at a tech company: engineering, design, product management, marketing, sales, business development, customer success and business operations.

Inside:

- The HUSTLE blueprint: do your homework, unlock openings, stand out, talk to people, level up and explain your story
- Where to find tech jobs, how to build a resume and portfolio, and a cold email that gets answered
- Study guides for engineers, designers, product managers, marketers and salespeople
- Interview questions with suggested answers for every role
- Everything you need to know about employee stock: options vs. RSUs, vesting, exercising and taxes
- A day in the life for each role, and how to break into venture capital

At the back: a glossary of startup terms, free training resources and real take-home interview projects to practice on.

This 2026 edition updates pay figures, company and product names, and removes resources that have closed. Part of the Ambitious Grads series.
